airport: broad paved aviation area with runway-like surfaces and sparse surrounding structures, distinguishing airport from footballfield by lacking clear sports-field markings and from industrial by emphasizing aviation pavement rather than factory compounds.
beach: bright shoreline region with a clear sand-water boundary, distinguishing beach from pond by broader coastal extent, from river by lacking a narrow winding channel, and from mountain by lacking rugged terrain relief.
bridge: narrow man-made crossing structure spanning water or land, distinguishing bridge from viaduct by a more localized crossing form, from port by lacking harbor-side infrastructure, and from pond by being a crossing rather than a compact water body.
commercial: organized urban built-up area with dense man-made structures and road access, distinguishing commercial from residential by larger and more regular building blocks, from parking by stronger building dominance, and from park by lacking large vegetation-dominant open space.
desert: dry barren land with sparse vegetation and homogeneous exposed-ground texture, distinguishing desert from farmland by lacking regular cultivated parcel patterns and from beach by lacking direct shoreline water contact.
farmland: regular cultivated land with visible plot boundaries and agricultural texture, distinguishing farmland from meadow by stronger man-made parcel organization and from desert by more structured crop-land pattern.
footballfield: rectangular sports field with clear field-like geometry and managed grass surface, distinguishing footballfield from meadow by stronger sports-ground structure, from airport by lacking broad paved aviation surfaces, and from railwaystation by lacking rail-line and station-like layouts.
forest: dense natural tree canopy with dark-green continuous vegetation texture, distinguishing forest from mountain by weaker relief and from pond by lacking a central water body.
industrial: factory-like compounds with utilitarian structures, storage areas, and production-oriented layout, distinguishing industrial from railwaystation by weaker rail-line concentration, from parking by having stronger building or yard structures, and from residential by larger production-oriented compounds.
meadow: broad natural grass-covered open area with soft vegetation texture, distinguishing meadow from footballfield by lacking formal sports-field geometry, from river by lacking a continuous water channel, and from farmland by lacking regular cultivated parcel boundaries.
mountain: rugged elevated terrain with clear relief, slope shadows, and irregular topographic texture, distinguishing mountain from forest by stronger terrain variation and from beach by lacking coastal sand-water boundaries.
park: planned green open space with vegetation and leisure-oriented layout, distinguishing park from pond by being land-dominant rather than water-dominant, from commercial by stronger vegetation presence, and from residential by weaker roof-pattern dominance.
parking: open paved area with vehicle-oriented organization and parking-row structure, distinguishing parking from industrial by lacking factory compounds, from residential by lacking repeated housing roofs, and from viaduct by lacking elevated linear crossing structure.
pond: small enclosed water body with compact shape and visible boundary, distinguishing pond from park by being water-dominant, from beach by lacking a broad coastal shoreline, and from river by lacking a long winding channel.
port: waterfront transport area with dock-side infrastructure and shore-adjacent logistics organization, distinguishing port from bridge by lacking a simple crossing structure, from river by stronger harbor-side man-made organization, and from railwaystation by emphasizing shoreline transport rather than rail-line concentration.
railwaystation: transport hub with concentrated rail lines and station-related structures, distinguishing railwaystation from industrial by clearer rail-line organization, from viaduct by lacking a simple elevated crossing form, and from footballfield by lacking sports-field geometry.
residential: built-up neighborhood with repeated housing roofs and regular living-area layout, distinguishing residential from commercial by smaller more repetitive roof structures, from industrial by weaker factory-like yard organization, and from parking by stronger housing-roof presence.
river: elongated natural watercourse with a continuous winding channel, distinguishing river from pond by stronger linear flow shape, from meadow by clear water dominance, and from beach by lacking a broad coastal shoreline.
viaduct: elongated elevated transport structure with visible grade-separated linear form, distinguishing viaduct from bridge by a more extended raised-traffic pattern, from residential by lacking repeated roof clusters, and from railwaystation by lacking concentrated station-like rail organization.
